title: Let X be a Noetherian scheme, i : Z → X a closed immersion with Z integral and eta its generic point
statement: Let X be a Noetherian scheme, i : Z → X a closed immersion with Z integral and eta its generic point. Let F be coherent on X and assume the maximal ideal of O_X,i(eta) kills its stalk. There exist a coherent module G on Z and a monomorphism beta : i_*G → F whose stalk at i(eta) is an isomorphism. This asserts only descent of the annihilated part, without any ideal-sum construction.

proof.text: The ideal module J of i is the kernel of the structure module mapping to its closed-subscheme pushforward. The closed-immersion annihilation theorem makes the latter quasi-coherent. Quasi-coherent kernels are quasi-coherent. The structure module is coherent by the finite-pushforward unit theorem applied to id_X, so the coherent-submodule theorem makes J coherent and hence finite type. The coherence criterion makes F quasi-coherent.

proof.text: Apply sections_annihilated_by_ideal to J and F to get a quasi-coherent submodule Fprime with mono inclusion iota. The coherent-submodule theorem makes Fprime coherent. The section range formula says that J kills every iota(s); injectivity of iota on sections, obtained from the limit-preserving sheaf-to-presheaf forgetful functor and module evaluation, says J kills s itself.

proof.text: The closed-immersion annihilation theorem makes the actual tensor pullback G of Fprime quasi-coherent and finite type and its adjunction unit eta invertible. A closed immersion is quasi-compact and locally of finite type; a Noetherian target therefore makes Z Noetherian. The coherence criterion makes G coherent. Define beta as eta inverse followed by iota, hence mono.

proof.text: For every ideal section a near xi, membership in i.ker says it vanishes on the image subscheme; the factorization of i through that subscheme implies i.app(a)=0. The germ/stalk-map formula implies i.stalkMap(eta)(germ(a))=0. If germ(a) were a unit, its image would be a unit, contradicting nontriviality of the source local ring. Thus germ(a) belongs to the ambient maximal ideal and hkill kills every element of F_xi by it. The annihilator stalk range formula makes iota_xi surjective, while the same theorem supplies its injectivity. Therefore iota_xi, and hence beta_xi, is an isomorphism.

lean.statement:
theorem coherent_generic_point_closed_descent {X Z : Scheme.{w}} [IsNoetherian X]
    (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsIntegral Z]
    (F : X.Modules) (hF : RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace F)
    (hkill : ∀ a ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk (i.base (genericPoint Z))),
      ∀ x : (RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace (i.base (genericPoint Z))).obj F,
        a • x = 0) :
    ∃ (G : Z.Modules), RingedSpace.IsCoherent Z.toRingedSpace G ∧
      ∃ (β : (pushforward i).obj G ⟶ F), Mono β ∧
        IsIso ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace
          (i.base (genericPoint Z))).map β)
